entries.note: System UI: status bar, notifications, lock screen and navigation. Disabling it leaves the device without a usable interface.
Telephony service: cellular calls, mobile data and SIM state. Disabling breaks all carrier connectivity.
Default AOSP launcher. Disabling the active launcher removes the home screen; only safe when another launcher is installed and set as default.
Settings app. Core device configuration surface; disabling removes access to system settings.
Package installer: handles APK install and uninstall sessions. Disabling breaks app installs.
Google Play Services: core APIs (location, push, auth, cast) used by most Google and third-party apps. Disabling breaks a large share of installed apps.
Google Services Framework: account and cloud-messaging plumbing underneath Play Services. Required for Google sign-in and push on GMS devices.
Telecom framework: routes and manages all voice and video calls. Calls fail without it.
ADB shell endpoint package. Disabling it severs the shell access this app itself relies on for package operations.
Telephony content provider: SMS/MMS storage and SIM records. Messaging apps depend on it.
Contacts content provider: shared contacts database used by the dialer, SMS apps and sync adapters.
MediaStore provider: indexed media database. Gallery and camera apps depend on it.
Settings content provider: backing store for all system settings. Core OS component.
External-storage (FUSE) provider. Shared-storage access for apps breaks without it.
Fused location provider: system location service consumed by apps and Play Services.
Play Store. Disabling stops app installs and updates from Play; safe only if you use an alternative store or sideload.
Android System WebView: embedded browser used by many apps. On Android 10+ Chrome can serve as the WebView provider; otherwise disabling breaks in-app web content.
Trichrome shared native library backing Chrome and WebView. Removing it breaks WebView rendering.
Google Phone dialer. Safe to disable only when another dialer handles calls and provides the in-call UI.
In-call UI for the AOSP dialer. Safe where a replacement dialer ships its own in-call screen; risky on devices relying on the AOSP dialer.
Text-to-speech engine. Accessibility services, navigation and reader apps depend on it.
First-boot setup wizard. Inert after setup completes, but a factory reset expects it; disabling before a reset can strand the setup flow.
GMS config updater (certificates, timezone and carrier config). Disabling can silently break Play Protect and network config refreshes.
System file picker (DocumentsUI). Many apps' file-chooser intents resolve here; disabling breaks them.
Bluetooth system service. Disabling kills Bluetooth; harmless only on devices where Bluetooth is never used.
NFC system service. Disabling kills NFC payments and tag reading; harmless only where NFC is unused.
System credential storage UI (VPN and Wi-Fi certificates). Disabling breaks certificate install flows.
Emergency information and SOS flows. Disabling removes emergency contact and medical info access from the lock screen.
Download provider used by the Play Store and browsers for managed downloads.
Google backup transport. Disabling stops cloud backup; on-device data is unaffected.
Carrier MMS service backing AOSP messaging. Third-party SMS apps may depend on it for MMS.
VPN consent dialogs. VPN apps cannot obtain user consent without it.
YouTube app. Fully removable; no OS component depends on it.
Facebook app. User-level app, safe to remove.
Preinstalled Meta app manager and updater stub. Safe to remove; it only manages Meta apps.
Preinstalled Meta system services stub (app installer helper). Safe to remove.
Preinstalled Meta background services. Safe to remove.
Instagram app. User-level, safe to remove.
Google Maps. Removable; alternatives exist.
Gmail. Removable; mail remains accessible via web or other clients.
Google Photos. Removable; the camera still works without it.
Chrome browser. Removable where another browser or WebView provider exists.
Play Games. Removable; games run without it.
Google TV (videos). Removable media app.
Google Meet. Removable.
Google Calendar. Removable.
Google Translate. Removable.
SIM Toolkit: carrier menu applets. Removing only hides carrier menus.
Print spooler. Only needed for printing.
AOSP calculator. Removable.
AOSP clock and alarms. Removable when replaced by another clock app.
Work-profile provisioning. Inert on devices without a work profile.
